# MVS Solves

> WebGL and motion engineering. Martin van Staden builds the motion layer most front-end developers turn down — raymarched GLSL, custom shaders, and scroll systems that feel attached to the page rather than towed behind it.

MVS Solves is a one-person studio in Brea, California, working on contract and white-label with agencies, studios, and product teams. Contact: martin@mvssolves.com.

Everything on this site is rendered live in the browser. There are no recordings, no video loops, and no pre-baked frames — each piece is running on the visitor's own GPU.

## Work

- [Rendered live](https://mvssolves.com/): raymarched signed-distance field in raw WebGL2 — no Three.js on the page. The hero object morphs between five primitives by interpolating distance functions, not by swapping meshes.
- [DESCENT](https://mvssolves.com/scroll/): an infinite corridor whose camera is driven entirely by scroll position.
- [INK](https://mvssolves.com/fluid/): a curl-noise fluid simulation, ping-ponged between framebuffers each frame.
- [SET IN MOTION](https://mvssolves.com/type/): kinetic typography built from mask reveals and difference blending, with no animation library.
- [SPRING FIELD](https://mvssolves.com/physics/): a particle field of thousands of damped springs sampled from rendered text.

## Capabilities

- Custom GLSL and raw WebGL2 — raymarching, signed distance fields, post-processing
- Scroll systems with GSAP and ScrollTrigger
- Three.js and React Three Fiber when a scene graph is the right tool
- React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind
- Performance work: adaptive resolution, frame budgets, Core Web Vitals

## How the work is engineered

- Everything degrades. No WebGL2, a weak GPU, or reduced-motion enabled and the layout still reads.
- Performance is measured, not hoped for. The shaders run an adaptive resolution governor that holds frame rate on unknown hardware.
- White-label is fine. The studio's name goes on the work.
